mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 4.5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 0.3% in the same month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3% AND PAYEMS falls > 0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 0.4% signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls > 0.4% AND HOUST falls > 0.4% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 1% and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising above 2% for three consecutive months, it signals a period of negative real interest rates, which boosts present value of future cash flows and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.0% AND CPIAUCSL rises > 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between real personal income (implied by PAYEMS and RSAFS growth) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, such that a monthly increase in both PAYEMS and RSAFS signals higher household purchasing power and drives positive short-term equity returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.3%) in at least 55% of triggered months.
